outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $5,200 to $24,000. Notes: The 120-300 day range and $5,200-$24,000 government cost range are the time and fees to obtain the approvals in the entitlement path when they are granted: Conditional Use Authorization (if required) and Health Permit to Operate. This is a time to approval, not a time to denial or withdrawal. The range assumes: (1) a CUA is required for the 3,995 sq ft size and takes 120-180 days from filing to Planning Commission hearing plus 30-day appeal period (typical CUA fee range $3,100-$15,000 depending on construction cost, with First Year Free waivers available for new storefront businesses); (2) health plan check takes 21-60 days ($828-$2,500, catalog:sf.health_plan_check) and the Health Permit to Operate takes 14-45 days ($470-$1,000, catalog:sf.health_permit) after construction is complete. If Planning confirms no CUA is required (e.g., the prior restaurant use at this address continues or the size trigger is waived), the timeline collapses to 35-105 days (health plan check plus permit to operate plus business registration) and government costs drop to $1,400-$3,700. Government costs shown exclude: building permit fees (a percentage of construction valuation, $800-$15,000 estimated, catalog:sf.building_permit), Fire Place of Assembly permit ($446-$1,500, catalog:sf.fire_place_of_assembly), sign permit ($300-$1,500, catalog:sf.sign_permit), state entity registration ($70-$150, catalog:ca.sos_entity_registration), business registration ($55-$700, catalog:sf.business_registration), FBN filing ($60-$120, catalog:sf.fictitious_business_name), food safety certifications ($107-$265 total, catalog:ca.food_safety_manager_cert and catalog:ca.food_handler_card for 20 employees), music licenses ($600-$5,000/year, catalog:us.ascap_license and catalog:us.bmi_license), and workers' compensation insurance premiums (percentage of payroll, not a government fee). Construction duration (storefront merger, kitchen build-out) is not included in this timeline; it runs in parallel with or after the CUA hearing and adds 2-6 months to the overall project schedule. The critical path item is confirming with Planning whether a CUA is required; that answer determines whether the timeline is 3-5 months (no CUA) or 6-10 months (CUA required).

The range assumes: (1) a CUA is required for the 3,995 sq ft size and takes 120-180 days from filing to Planning Commission hearing plus 30-day appeal period (typical CUA fee range $3,100-$15,000 depending on construction cost, with First Year Free waivers available for new storefront businesses); (2) health plan check takes 21-60 days ($828-$2,500, catalog:sf.health_plan_check) and the Health Permit to Operate takes 14-45 days ($470-$1,000, catalog:sf.health_permit) after construction is complete. If Planning confirms no CUA is required (e.g., the prior restaurant use at this address continues or the size trigger is waived), the timeline collapses to 35-105 days (health plan check plus permit to operate plus business registration) and government costs drop to $1,400-$3,700. Government costs shown exclude: building permit fees (a percentage of construction valuation, $800-$15,000 estimated, catalog:sf.building_permit), Fire Place of Assembly permit ($446-$1,500, catalog:sf.fire_place_of_assembly), sign permit ($300-$1,500, catalog:sf.sign_permit), state entity registration ($70-$150, catalog:ca.sos_entity_registration), business registration ($55-$700, catalog:sf.business_registration), FBN filing ($60-$120, catalog:sf.fictitious_business_name), food safety certifications ($107-$265 total, catalog:ca.food_safety_manager_cert and catalog:ca.food_handler_card for 20 employees), music licenses ($600-$5,000/year, catalog:us.ascap_license and catalog:us.bmi_license), and workers' compensation insurance premiums (percentage of payroll, not a government fee). Construction duration (storefront merger, kitchen build-out) is not included in this timeline; it runs in parallel with or after the CUA hearing and adds 2-6 months to the overall project schedule. The critical path item is confirming with Planning whether a CUA is required; that answer determines whether the timeline is 3-5 months (no CUA) or 6-10 months (CUA required).
outcomes.note: The cited records show only health plan check (21-60 days, $828-$2,500) and health permit (14-45 days, $470-$1,000); they do not contain CUA timing or fees that drive the stated 120-300 day and $5,200-$24,000 ranges.
